concerns.text: T126 (Error Budget Analysis) requires decomposing 'Geometry Optimization Error' and 'Basis Set Error' into a 'Total Error Budget'. The spec (FR-004, FR-005) and plan only mandate a paired t-test comparing model errors (MAE) between Semi-Empirical and DFT methods. There is no requirement to quantify or report the specific error contributions of the geometry optimization step or basis set truncation. This task introduces unrequested analysis (scope creep) that violates the constraint of implementing only what the spec demands.

T125 (Validation Against Physical Constants) mandates verifying 'bond lengths > 0' and 'energies < 0' and logging 'Physical Invalidity'. While FR-002 and Edge Cases mention retrying on convergence/physical invalidity (HOMO >= LUMO), the spec does not require a separate validation script to check general physical constants like bond lengths or bound-state energies as a distinct deliverable. This task adds a new verification layer not present in the spec's acceptance criteria, potentially violating the 'no silent constitution drift' principle by introducing unmandated validation logic.

T011 (Confounds Analysis) specifies checking for a 'SMILES' column (uppercase) in `data/raw/barrier_dataset.csv`. The spec (Data Model) explicitly defines the column as 'smiles' (lowercase). This task description relaxes the strict case-sensitivity required by the data model, creating a semantic mismatch that will cause runtime failure or silent data loss if the implementation follows the task text literally. The task must be corrected to match the spec's exact column naming convention.

T020a (Subset Selection) includes a logic branch: 'If the count of available molecules is < 90% of the target... log a REPRESENATIVENESS_WARNING'. The spec (FR-004) and plan require a stratified subset but do not define a 90% threshold or a specific warning mechanism for subset size reduction due to convergence failures. Introducing a specific '90%' threshold and a custom warning log entry constitutes a silent relaxation of the strict stratification requirement by adding an unverified heuristic not present in the spec.

T121 requires updating reports to 'Explicitly state that quantum calculations... are computational models and not measurements' and citing specific reviewers (Curie, Franklin, Einstein). While the Constitution (FR-030) requires addressing reviewer concerns, the spec (US2, FR-005) does not mandate a specific textual declaration distinguishing 'calculation' from 'measurement' in the output reports. This task risks violating the 'Single Source of Truth' principle by embedding specific reviewer rhetoric into the deliverable schema without a corresponding requirement in the spec.
